steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The cognitive approach focuses on internal mental processes: perception, memory, thinking, problem-solving, attention, and language. It treats the mind like a computer: input (sensory information) -> processing (thinking) -> output (behaviour). | Key Fact: Schemas: mental frameworks that organise knowledge and expectations. They help us process information quickly but can lead to biases and errors. Schemas develop through experience and affect how we interpret new information (e.g. Bartlett's 'War of the Ghosts' study showed participants distorted a story to fit their cultural schemas). | Key Fact: Cognitive biases: systematic errors in thinking that affect decisions and judgements.
